ticket.title: Telemetry log has no retention, rotation or aggregates

task.title: Telemetry log has no retention, rotation or aggregates

events.description:
FILED 2026-11-08, because no retention ticket existed - an earlier handover note in this session named GB-341 as the
retention ticket, and GB-341 is "A Verified task cannot be reopened". That was my error, recorded here so the next
reader does not go looking for a ticket that was never written.

MEASURED STATE, one session after every tool started emitting: 75 spans, 18,147 bytes, ~242 bytes per span, in a single
append-only file at `.gaugeblock/telemetry/events.jsonl`. The directory holds nothing else.

WHAT THAT IMPLIES, and the shape of the problem: at 242 bytes a span, a million spans is ~240 MB in one file that every
tool appends to and nothing ever reads back selectively. Nothing rotates it, nothing aggregates it, and nothing prunes
it. The log is the only place a run's history exists, so deleting it loses evidence - which is why this is a design
ticket rather than a cron job.

WHAT RETENTION HAS TO KEEP, which is the hard part and the reason to decide before the file is large:
  * the panel needs recent spans at full fidelity;
  * `storypole handoff` wants spans by task key (GB-309), so old spans are not automatically junk;
  * law 12 wants performance claims to persist, and a rotated-away measurement is a claim with no backing;
  * a trace that spans a rotation boundary must not be torn in half, or a duration computed across it becomes a lie.

CANDIDATE SHAPES, none chosen: size-based rotation with an aggregate sidecar (counts and duration percentiles per
binary/day, kept forever, raw spans aged out); date-partitioned files with a retention window; or keeping raw spans and
adding an index so the file is cheap to query rather than cheap to store.

The measurement above is warm and single-machine - the numbers are real, the projection is arithmetic, not a benchmark.
